hypotheses.reasoning: GET /search 500s at web-bff are the alert, but web-bff only reports 'upstream search-api returned 500'. search-api fails because catalog-svc /products/batch returns 500 with 'storage write failed' (#1273, #1463). catalog-svc is failing its synchronous writes to S3 (us-east-1, bucket search-artifacts-prod) with AWS-side errors: 503 ServiceUnavailable (#1231, #1431) and InternalError 500 with request IDs (#1285, #1384). The aws-sdk then exhausts its retry quota (46 failed attempts in 60s, #1323). The errors are fast 5xx responses carrying AWS request IDs, which points to a cloud storage outage rather than a timeout or a bad config on our side. The first S3 error (#1231, 20:37:52) lines up with the onset of the search failures. The auth/IdP timeouts (#886, #1109) and account-svc pool saturation mainly drive /login 503s and are a separate chain that does not explain /search. Metrics-agent drops are a side effect of the logging pipeline and are not causal.

Secondary reading: the SDK retry storm against S3 (retry quota exhausted, #1323) amplifies a small storage blip into a full /search failure, because catalog-svc writes synchronously on the read path. Search-api's 'storage write failed' errors and the web-bff 500s (#1226) are downstream of this amplification. If the S3 outage were ruled out, this would become the leading hypothesis.

verdict.recommendedAction: Confirm the AWS S3 us-east-1 status and incident feed for 20:37–20:45Z. Mitigate by taking the synchronous S3 write off the /products/batch and /search read path, or by serving from cache/last-good artifacts, and by failing open when the write fails. Cap or back off the aws-sdk retries in catalog-svc to stop the retry storm. Separately, investigate the auth-svc IdP timeouts (#886, #1009, #1109) that are causing /login 503s. Once S3 recovers, replay the failed artifact writes (p-6290, p-6313, p-6338, p-6356) if they are needed.

hypotheses.reasoning: GET /search 500s at web-bff are the alert, but web-bff only reports 'upstream search-api returned 500'. search-api fails because catalog-svc /products/batch returns 500 with 'storage write failed' (#1273, #1463). catalog-svc is failing its synchronous writes to S3 (us-east-1, bucket search-artifacts-prod) with AWS-side errors: 503 ServiceUnavailable (#1231, #1431) and InternalError 500 with request IDs (#1285, #1384). The aws-sdk then exhausts its retry quota (46 failed attempts in 60s, #1323). The errors are fast 5xx responses carrying AWS request IDs, which points to a cloud storage outage rather than a timeout or a bad config on our side. The first S3 error (#1231, 20:37:52) lines up with the onset of the search failures. The auth/IdP timeouts (#886, #1109) and account-svc pool saturation mainly drive /login 503s and are a separate chain that does not explain /search. Metrics-agent drops are a side effect of the logging pipeline and are not causal.

Secondary reading: the SDK retry storm against S3 (retry quota exhausted, #1323) amplifies a small storage blip into a full /search failure, because catalog-svc writes synchronously on the read path. Search-api's 'storage write failed' errors and the web-bff 500s (#1226) are downstream of this amplification. If the S3 outage were ruled out, this would become the leading hypothesis.

input.recommendedAction: Confirm the AWS S3 us-east-1 status and incident feed for 20:37–20:45Z. Mitigate by taking the synchronous S3 write off the /products/batch and /search read path, or by serving from cache/last-good artifacts, and by failing open when the write fails. Cap or back off the aws-sdk retries in catalog-svc to stop the retry storm. Separately, investigate the auth-svc IdP timeouts (#886, #1009, #1109) that are causing /login 503s. Once S3 recovers, replay the failed artifact writes (p-6290, p-6313, p-6338, p-6356) if they are needed.
